title: 2. What the Company Does: Segments, Revenue Mix & Concrete Examples
summary_box: Post-demerger listed INDIAGLYCO retains Bio-based Specialties & Performance Chemicals (BSPC: bio-MEG/DEG/TEG, glycol ethers, green solvents), Industrial Gases (liquid O2, N2, Argon, CO2, and IGL-SteriGas), and a 49% stake in Clariant IGL Specialty Chemicals. Continuing revenue runs at ~₹357–362 Cr/quarter (~₹1,440 Cr annualized). That compares with FY26's pre-demerger ₹4,211 Cr conglomerate base, which included Potable Spirits, Bio-Fuels, and Ennature Biopharma.

epigraph.quote: To value what remains after a corporate split, first draw the boundary line in thick ink—nothing confuses an analyst faster than valuing yesterday's perimeter on today's income statement.
epigraph.author: Forensic Accounting Principle

web_blocks.html: Before September 2026, India Glycols Limited operated as a four-engine conglomerate. It generated ₹4,211 Cr in FY26 consolidated sales and ₹649 Cr in operating profit (15% OPM) [1][9]. Under the NCLT-approved Composite Scheme of Arrangement (Appointed Date April 1, 2026; Effective Date September 1, 2026), two engines moved into standalone companies [2][3][8]. IGL Spirits Limited took Potable Spirits and Bio-Fuels/Ethanol on a 1:1 share entitlement. Ennature Bio Pharma Limited took Nutraceuticals, Plant-based APIs, and Biopolymers/Natural Gums on a 1:3 share entitlement [3][8][14].

Consequently, from Q1 FY27 onward, listed INDIAGLYCO is a pure-play industrial and green-chemistry entity. It rests on three remaining pillars: (1) Bio-based Specialties & Performance Chemicals (BSPC), (2) Industrial Gases, and (3) a 49% equity-accounted stake in Clariant IGL Specialty Chemicals Pvt Ltd [4][10][12]. In Q1 FY27 and Q2 FY27, continuing consolidated revenue stood at ₹357.08 Cr and ₹362.42 Cr. Those quarters produced ₹39 Cr of quarterly operating profit (11% OPM) and ₹33 Cr / ₹24 Cr in quarterly net profit [1][4][21].

web_blocks.takeaway: Roughly 67% of FY26 revenue (Potable Spirits, Bio-Fuels, and Ennature) exited the listed perimeter on April 1, 2026. What remains is a ~₹1,440 Cr/year continuing-operations chemical and gases platform.

web_blocks.html: Segment 1 — Bio-based Specialties & Performance Chemicals (BSPC, ~96% of continuing revenue): IGL converts renewable ethanol from molasses and grain at Kashipur and Gorakhpur into bio-ethylene and bio-ethylene oxide (Bio-EO). Downstream, it produces Bio-MEG, Bio-DEG, Bio-TEG, Glycol Ethers, and Glycol Ether Acetates [10][19]. Concrete End-to-End Customer Example: Consider a European automotive coatings formulator or global beverage packaging brand seeking to cut Scope 3 carbon emissions. Rather than buying fossil-route butyl glycol acetate made from Middle Eastern naphtha, it contracts IGL Kashipur for bio-based glycol ether acetates certified for 100% renewable carbon content. IGL dehydrates bio-ethanol into ethylene, reacts it into Bio-EO, synthesizes the glycol ether, and esterifies it into acetate. It then ships ISO-tank containers via Mundra or Nhava Sheva to Rotterdam. That route captures a green specialty spread while avoiding the low-margin traded chemicals business management exited in FY25–FY26 [6][10][19].

Segment 2 — Clariant IGL Specialty Chemicals JV (49% Equity Associate): Clariant formed this JV in June 2021 by investing ₹587.74 Cr for 51% of IGL's Bio-EO derivatives unit inside Kashipur [11]. Concrete End-to-End Customer Example: When a multinational personal-care or home-care FMCG company formulates a 'bio-based' shampoo or detergent in India or Southeast Asia, it needs renewable ethoxylates and surfactants. IGL pipes Bio-EO directly across the fence at Kashipur under a long-term supply contract. The Clariant IGL JV ethoxylates that feedstock using Clariant's global formulations and sells to the FMCG buyer [10][11]. IGL earns a steady feedstock margin on Bio-EO sales, plus 49% of the JV's net profit and substantial cash dividends [10][11].

Segment 3 — Industrial Gases & IGL-SteriGas (~3%–4% of continuing revenue, ~₹46–47 Cr/yr): IGL operates an Air Separation Unit (ASU) and liquid CO2 recovery plants at Kashipur. The unit sells 67,000+ MT annually of liquid oxygen (including medical grade), liquid nitrogen, argon, food-grade LCO2, and IGL-SteriGas sterilization mixtures [12]. Concrete End-to-End Customer Example: A surgical-disposables and catheter manufacturer in NCR or Baddi cannot autoclave heat-sensitive plastic syringes. It buys cylinders of IGL-SteriGas, which IGL blends in-house from captive EO and LCO2, to sterilize medical kits at low temperature. That gives IGL a sticky, regulatory-cleared industrial niche with >20% EBITDA margins [12].

Context on Demerged Verticals (What Exited in 2026): Through March 2026, historical financials in Chapter 6 also included three exited businesses. First, Potable Spirits held market-leading country liquor brands like Bunty Bubbly in UP and Uttarakhand, IMFL brands like Macintosh, and long-term bottling contracts for Bacardi and Amrut Distilleries at Kashipur [13]. Second, Bio-Fuels supplied grain and molasses ethanol to oil marketing companies under India's E20 mandate [9]. Third, Ennature Biopharma produced plant-based APIs like Thiocolchicoside and nicotine derivatives, lutein nutraceuticals, and guar gum biopolymers [14]. None of these three verticals remain inside listed INDIAGLYCO's P&L after April 1, 2026 [2][3][8].

web_blocks.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
paragraphs: Notice how sharply the margin profile shifts once you draw the post-demerger boundary. Pre-demerger INDIAGLYCO posted 14%–17% OPM because Potable Spirits (~21.4% EBIT margin) masked the cyclicality of commodity glycols. Post-demerger INDIAGLYCO printed 11% OPM in Q1 and Q2 FY27.

That 11% margin is the honest baseline of the standalone BSPC + Industrial Gases business before factoring in the 49% Clariant JV profit share below the operating line. Whether BSPC can climb back toward 13%–15% OPM through higher glycol-ether utilization and zero low-margin trading is the central operational question.

book_paragraphs: If you walked onto the trading floor or opened a financial screener in November 2026 without reading the NCLT order, you would think India Glycols had lost two-thirds of its customers overnight. Revenue fell from ₹1,092 Cr in the September 2025 quarter to ₹362 Cr in the September 2026 quarter. Yet not a single reactor in Kashipur was shut down, and not a single major chemical contract was lost.

What happened is that on September 1, 2026—retroactive to April 1, 2026—India Glycols formally severed its consumer and pharma limbs from its industrial chemical core. Every shareholder received one share of IGL Spirits Limited for every share held, taking away the lucrative Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand country liquor empire, the Bacardi and Amrut bottling lines, and ₹1,470 Cr of ethanol biofuel sales. They also received one share of Ennature Bio Pharma Limited for every three shares held, taking away the Thiocolchicoside, nicotine, lutein, and guar gum business.

So what exactly are you and I looking at when we analyze listed INDIAGLYCO today? Three tightly integrated industrial pieces centered on Kashipur and Gorakhpur. First is Bio-based Specialties and Performance Chemicals—converting renewable alcohol into green MEG, DEG, TEG, and higher-margin glycol ethers and acetates for global coatings, brake-fluid, and sustainable packaging buyers. Second is a quiet gem: Industrial Gases, selling over 67,000 metric tonnes a year of liquid oxygen, nitrogen, carbon dioxide, and IGL-SteriGas sterilization mixtures to North Indian hospitals and medical-device makers at over 20% EBITDA margins.

Third, sitting just below the operating line as an associate, is the 49% stake in Clariant IGL Specialty Chemicals. India Glycols pipes bio-ethylene oxide across the fence in Kashipur; Clariant turns it into green surfactants for global personal-care giants and sends 49% of the profits and hefty dividends back to India Glycols.

Knowing that boundary is everything. From April 2026 onward, you are no longer underwriting a liquor-and-ethanol conglomerate. You are underwriting a ₹1,440 Cr-run-rate green specialty chemical and industrial gas business with a world-class Swiss joint-venture partner.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
paragraphs: Separating Potable Spirits from BSPC removes a huge valuation distraction, but it also removes a cash-cow buffer. In Chapter 3, we trace how every ₹100 of revenue flows through this chemical complex—and how working capital and capex behave when molasses, grain, and crude oil all move at once.
